about.title: Corte Madera Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Corte Madera is a small town, fewer than ten thousand residents settled between the bay and the base of Mount Tamalpais, and when a family here loses someone, the absence is felt on quiet streets and in familiar places. Public records for 2025 show 48 injury collisions and 61 people hurt on local roads, with US-101, Tamalpais Drive and Paradise Drive carrying the largest share of reported crashes; those same records list no traffic deaths that year. Wrongful death claims in Marin County do not only follow collisions, though. They can arise from unsafe premises, medical mistakes, defective products and workplace incidents as well. Under California law, a spouse, domestic partner or child usually holds the first right to bring the claim, and a two-year clock begins on the date of death. The claim is civil, entirely separate from anything a prosecutor may or may not decide to do. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Corte Madera families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency, so you can grieve while someone else tracks the deadlines and paperwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Corte Madera Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, giving a spouse, domestic partner and children priority before other dependents or heirs. An attorney can tell your family quickly whether and how you qualify.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general filing window is two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. Getting connected early protects that window.

items.title: Full picture of recoverable losses
items.desc: Beyond funeral and burial costs, California allows recovery for lost financial support and for the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed on US-101 near Corte Madera. Does the shorter government deadline apply?
items.answer: It might, and that is exactly why it is worth asking now. US-101 is a state highway, so if a road condition or public vehicle played a role, a claim against a government entity must be presented on a much shorter timeline than the standard two years. An attorney can review the collision report and determine whether Caltrans, the Town of Corte Madera, Marin County or only a private driver is potentially responsible.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, with its own deadline. The criminal case is brought by the state and does not compensate your family, while the civil claim exists to address your losses. Many families pursue both at the same time.

items.question: What does it cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. We are a free connection service, not a law firm, and we match you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases in Marin County. Those attorneys work on contingency, which means no fee unless there is a recovery for your family.
